record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares Adam with L2 regularization to decoupled weight decay and reports held-out error results, testing how an optimizer and regularization choice affect generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper's derivations and cited results from other researchers are not rows. Figure 1's learning-rate schedule comparisons are described qualitatively; the retained rows focus on the explicit 15% relative test-error improvement reported for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out image-classification performance across Adam, momentum SGD, and decoupled-weight-decay variants. It is itself the V4 original source arXiv:1711.05101, so no verdict labels are assigned.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: decoupled weight decay substantially improves Adam's generalization and makes it competitive with momentum SGD in the tested image-classification settings. The authors also report improved anytime performance from warm restarts and explicitly leave broader task validation for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares Adam and AdamW on image-classification networks using training and test error; it does not reproduce the broader optimizer comparison across tasks in Wilson et al.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error advantage varies with the learning-rate schedule; the paper says decoupled weight decay outperforms L2 regularization across fixed, step-drop, and cosine schedules, with larger differences for better schedules.
record.problems: The main experiments are image-classification experiments; the authors say the results need verification on a wider range of tasks. The 15% comparisons are reported without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other numeric main-paper rows were left out. Figure 1's learning-rate schedule comparisons and Figure 2's hyperparameter landscapes are discussed qualitatively but are not included as separate rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width scaling beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, word-level language models, adaptive optimizers other than Adam, broader optimizer hyperparameter tuning, and switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons; the experiments use batch size 128 throughout.
The effect of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.

missing.what: For the 26 2x96d ResNet, AdamW has lower test error than Adam at similar training loss on both datasets. This separates improved generalization from improved convergence and is not captured by the aggregate 15% rows.
missing.locator: Section 4.3, Figure 3 bottom right; Appendix D, SuppFigure 4

missing.what: The corrected Adam variants close most of the performance gap to SGDWR on CIFAR-10 and reach comparable performance on ImageNet32x32. Record these direct comparisons with SGD rather than only AdamW versus Adam.

record.verdict_notes: This is an original source for V4, not independent corroboration. Figures 1 and 2 are explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out, so their schedule and hyperparameter comparisons are not listed as missing. Section 4.5 reports other groups' results and should not supply rows attributed to this study's own experiments.

versions.untested_parts: The paper focuses on image classification, Adam versus AdamW, and weight-decay variants. It does not test the broader optimizer benchmarks, broad hyperparameter tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language models described in the version.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

rows.subject: 26 2x64d ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam with L2 regularization against AdamW with decoupled weight decay.
rows.value: AdamW achieved 15% relative improvement in test error compared to Adam.
rows.note: The paper reports this comparison at the default learning rate of 0.001.
rows.check: The 15% relative improvement is correctly reported and bears on V4's weight-decay recovery clause. Specify Top-1 test error, initial learning rate 0.001, and cosine annealing. Section 4.4 and Figure 4's caption do not establish the recorded 26 2x64d architecture or 11.6M parameter count; verify these rather than inferring them from the base-network description.
